parsed.explanation: The combined regime does not criminalise trans identity, but it imposes state-made exposure at the two points a visitor cannot avoid: the border and government buildings. National entry guidance invites refusal where appearance, marker or records diverge and contemplates a permanent fraud finding; foreign governments have issued advisories and reported detentions. National orders bar trans people from sex-congruent facilities in government-funded buildings, and national immigration and prison custody carry documented abuse. This division adds no facility ban or criminalisation and no adult care prohibition, but its hate-crime statute excludes gender identity and statewide accommodation protection is absent. Courts have enjoined several orders and litigation continues, so typical severity is refusal, exclusion, discrimination and invasive screening, with harmful custody a documented but lower-probability tail.

entry_documents.exposure: National rules restrict markers to M/F; a February 2025 cable directs refusal where documents or records diverge or doubt arises about sex, and contemplates a material-misrepresentation lifetime ineligibility finding; athletes banned. Advisories and detentions of foreign citizens reported.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; fraud finding requires four elements and is never automatic; litigation ongoing; legal-aid FAQ available. No dossier rule rejecting foreign-issued markers.
entry_documents.interaction: A foreign passport presented at a national port meets national adjudication guidance; officer discretion at post or port decides, with little real-time remedy for a refused visitor.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy from 2026 removes hormones, cuts hair and substitutes psychiatric treatment; immigration custody shows forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse; trans prisoner counts no longer published.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; several executive orders enjoined by courts; state protective-order framework extended in 2021.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A document discrepancy at entry can escalate into immigration custody, where the documented abusive practices apply; state custody would not fund transition care.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity, reaching federal buildings, airports and parks inside this division; four states criminalise facility use via trespass, with a documented handcuffed arrest and men's-ward holding.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no facility ban and no criminalisation since the 2017 repeal; no statute bars identity-congruent use. Local ordinances cover part of the population.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federally owned and funded buildings follow the national bar regardless of local tolerance; state facilities are currently unaffected, though a 2025 bathroom bill was revived.

care_services.exposure: State law bars puberty blockers, hormones and surgery for under-18s and bars state funds for minors and prisoners; 27 states ban minors' care; national justice department subpoenaed hospital records of patients under 19; reimbursement rule pending.
care_services.protection: Adult visitor care is not prohibited; hospital patients'-rights and designated-visitor statutes apply; no documented seizure or refusal regime aimed at adult visitors.
care_services.interaction: A family seeking care for a minor meets provider refusal and possible record inquiry; an adult visitor's own medication is not documented as confiscated at the border.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups among priorities; justice-department reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology'; schools investigating social transition; advocates allege genocide precursors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy states powers will not target mere disagreement; the memo does not use the phrase as a reward criterion; courts have enjoined several orders; national hate-crime coverage exists.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Rhetoric raises the stakes if a visitor is swept into an investigation, but no prosecution of a trans visitor on this basis is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors' gender-affirming care banned here and in 27 states; national order frames such care as mutilation and directs investigation of facilitating teachers; parental-notification school law applies to enrolled students.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented penalty on visiting parents for a child's identity; public funding of conversion therapy barred; visitation statute.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care refusal and possible state record inquiry; school-notification duties do not reach a short-stay visitor's child.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: State hate-crime statute covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation, so bias assaults may not be charged as bias crimes; no statewide accommodation protection; trans-specific violence rate explicitly not established.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus the capital outlaw identity discrimination; city and county ordinances cover roughly 30 per cent of residents.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse turns on locality: visitors outside ordinance areas have thin civil remedy, while a national bias charge remains discretionary.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport restrictions took effect after the national court declined to block them; fraud findings are permanent with limited waiver; several measures remain in force pending appeal.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have enjoined multiple orders; a civil-liberties union suit with seven plaintiffs is live; legal-aid guidance exists; appeals and injunctions have produced relief in some cases.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Judicial relief is real but prospective and slow; a short-stay visitor usually departs before any remedy matures, so protection operates as climate more than as recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Meridia's transport police extort travellers, confiscate documents, use overnight cells and seal logs, with oversight dismissing complaints. Here no police extortion or raid pattern is documented, no cross-dressing or administrative-building offence exists, and courts actively enjoin measures, so this jurisdiction sits clearly above that tier despite shared document-driven discretion.

Vellandra bars entry categorically to noncompliant trans visitors with quasi-automatic, unreviewable exclusion. Here refusal is conditioned on document discrepancy or reasonable doubt, existing X passports stay valid and litigation is live, so exclusion is less universal and less final — but the fraud pathway keeps it materially below neutral.

Kestrel Isles offers discretionary secondary screening, refused admission and slow appeals, but no other exposure. This jurisdiction matches that border tier and adds facility exclusion in federally funded buildings, minors' care bans and documented custody abuse, so it rates below it.

Meridia's entry regime assumes trained officers, brief detention, tribunal appeals and compensation. Here screening guidance treats divergence as suspicion, national equality protection is absent and custody conditions are documented as harmful, so this jurisdiction sits far below that anchor.

parsed.synthesis: The operative sequence runs from document presentation to facility access to care. A visitor whose marker, appearance or records diverge meets national adjudication guidance that permits refusal and contemplates permanent ineligibility; some foreign governments now warn against travel. If admitted, federally owned or funded buildings apply the national birth-sex facility bar even where this division's repealed ban leaves state facilities open. A travelling family seeking care for a minor meets a state prohibition plus national record demands. Recourse exists — courts have enjoined several orders and hate-crime coverage is national — but it is slow, locality-dependent and largely unavailable within a short stay, leaving severity concentrated in refusal, exclusion and discrimination rather than prosecution.
